input.summary: Full ledger review completed for p17. I traced all 22 claims (independent claims 1, 13, 18 and dependent claims 2-12, 14-17, 19-22) limitation by limitation, all 27 reference numerals in draft/numerals.md, every numbered part and relationship in the title, field, summary, detailed description and abstract, and all seven figure briefs (FIG. 1-7) including their per-figure numeral lists and the 3-3 and 5-5 section-line designations, against the affirmative inventor passages in input/disclosure.md and the (truncated) USER passage in input/conversation.md; input/brief.md was used only for formalities (title, applicant/inventor, no priority claim, no federal support, apparatus+method claims, no means-plus-function, preserved terminology rail / fixed fence / guide carriage / drill bushing / clamp knob / clamping shoe / spacer plate / pointer / center index / sight notch, all of which are used consistently). Substantively, the claim set, description and abstract are traceable: rail with flat lower face, upper face, through longitudinal slot and printed distance marks; fence at the first end, perpendicular, downwardly projecting portion, two screws in two corresponding holes, reversible to the opposite longitudinal side with the marked face still visible; removable spacer plate with parallel faces changing setback without changing separation; two separate carriages with anti-rotation keys, cylindrical hardened replaceable bushings whose bores pass completely through and register with the slot and are parallel and perpendicular to the lower face; clamp knob, threaded shank through slot, clamping shoe below the rail; two pointers each aligned with its own bore axis and read against the same marks, their difference being the center-to-center spacing; transverse center index at the midpoint; shallow V-shaped sight notch in the second end aligned with the index; the recited method sequence; the rigid polymer or metal materials with hardened-metal bushings; and the no motor / battery / sensor / network limitation. Numerals are one-to-one with parts, every numeral appears in at least one figure brief, no numeral carries two meanings, no drafting note, placeholder, open question or unresolved alternative remains, and section line 3-3 (FIG. 3, through the second guide carriage 70) and line 5-5 (FIG. 5, through the first guide carriage 50) use the same designations in the Brief Description, the source-view brief FIG. 2 and the resulting views. Five defects were verified. (1) Critical: the FIG. 7 brief places the transverse center index 24 in the strip between one long side of the rail and the neighbouring long side of the longitudinal slot 16, "so that it stands clear of the longitudinal slot 16" — an untraced relative location conveying technical substance, which also conflicts with the description's statement that the index "runs across the rail 10". (2) Major: the FIG. 7 brief is geometrically self-contradictory, putting the sight notch 26 at the second end of the rail while making the centerline 94 and the index alignment run transversely across the band at the midpoint, so the notch cannot lie on the alignment the same brief assigns it. (3) Major: the FIG. 4 brief states that the slot "passes through the rail 10 from its upper side to the lower face 14" and simultaneously that it "appears in this view as a narrow opening in the upper side of the rail 10", an untraced end-view runout/geometry statement that contradicts claim 1 and the description. (4) Minor: numeral 16 is used in the FIG. 4 body text but is absent from that figure's numeral list. (5) Minor: FIG. 1 depicts "a plain round body" above each carriage with no reference numeral and no counterpart in the description's FIG. 1 discussion. Every other structure, relationship, result, material, shape, position, connection, operating condition and variant in the text and figure briefs traced to an exact affirmative inventor passage; Background prior-art characterizations were left to the separate prior-art trace.

findings.title: FIG. 7 assigns the transverse center index an undisclosed position relative to the longitudinal slot
findings.where: figures/FIG-7.md, paragraph describing transverse center index 24 (cross-check draft/08-detailed-description.md, paragraph beginning "Referring to FIG. 7")
findings.detail: The figure brief fixes where the center index sits across the rail's width relative to the slot, stating that it occupies only the strip on one side and does not reach the slot. That is a relative location conveying technical substance (whether the centering mark is a full-width transverse mark or a one-sided mark offset from the slot bears on how the index is sighted against the centerline), and no inventor passage discloses it. The disclosure says only that the rail has a transverse center index at its midpoint; it says nothing about the index's width, its side, or its relation to the slot. The figure statement also contradicts the description, which says the index "runs across the rail 10 transverse to the length of the rail 10".
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-7.md): "It runs transverse to the length of the rail 10 and occupies the strip of upper surface between one long side of the band and the neighbouring long side of the longitudinal slot 16, so that it stands clear of the longitudinal slot 16." Nearest inventor passage (input/disclosure.md): "The rail has a transverse center index at its midpoint." No affirmative passage in the disclosure or in the USER text of input/conversation.md describes the index's extent across the rail or its position relative to the longitudinal slot.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-7.md, delete the clause "and occupies the strip of upper surface between one long side of the band and the neighbouring long side of the longitudinal slot 16, so that it stands clear of the longitudinal slot 16" so the sentence reads: "A transverse center index 24 is a single straight stroke of visible thickness lying on the upper surface of the rail 10 in the left part of the fragment, well away from the second end of the rail 10. It runs transverse to the length of the rail 10."

findings.title: FIG. 7 brief specifies an alignment the sight notch cannot occupy
findings.where: figures/FIG-7.md, paragraphs describing sight notch 26 and centerline 94
findings.detail: Within one figure brief the center index is placed transversely in the left part of the fragment at the rail's midpoint, the centerline 94 is placed on that same transverse alignment (two collinear segments emerging from the two long sides of the band), and the sight notch 26 is placed in the second end of the rail yet is said to lie on that same alignment. A notch at the end of the band cannot lie on a line that crosses the band transversely at the midpoint, so the three statements cannot be drawn together. The description and claims require the index, the notch and the centerline to share one alignment, so the figure brief must depict a single, achievable alignment.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-7.md): "A transverse center index 24 ... lying on the upper surface of the rail 10 in the left part of the fragment, well away from the second end of the rail 10."; "A sight notch 26 is a shallow V-shaped notch formed in the second end of the rail 10, shown schematically, and lying on the alignment of the transverse center index 24."; "A centerline 94 is a straight line drawn on the workpiece 90 alone, on the same alignment as the transverse center index 24. It appears as two collinear segments of that one line, one segment starting at each long side of the band and running outward across the workpiece 90 away from the band." Supporting inventor passage (input/disclosure.md): "A shallow V-shaped sight notch is formed in the second end of the rail and aligned with the center index. The user can align the center index and the sight notch with a pencil centerline on the workpiece."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-7.md, replace the centerline paragraph with: "A centerline 94 is a straight line drawn on the workpiece 90 alone, lying on the one common alignment of the transverse center index 24 and the sight notch 26. The line runs lengthwise of the rail 10 beneath the band and emerges beyond the second end of the rail 10 at the sight notch 26, the portion beneath the band being hidden by the rail 10." and change the index sentence to end "...transverse to the length of the rail 10, its midpoint lying on that same alignment." so that index 24, notch 26 and centerline 94 all lie on one straight, drawable alignment.

findings.title: FIG. 4 depicts the longitudinal slot as an opening only in the upper side of the rail
findings.where: figures/FIG-4.md, paragraph describing the rail 10 and longitudinal slot 16
findings.detail: The sentence is self-contradictory and contradicts the rest of the application: it first says the slot passes through the rail from the upper side to the lower face 14, then says that in this end-on elevation it appears as "a narrow opening in the upper side of the rail 10", which depicts a blind groove rather than a through slot. How the slot terminates or runs out at the rail end, and whether it breaks the upper side only, is an end-face geometry statement that the disclosure never makes, and the through character of the slot is required by claim 1 and by the shank and drill-bit paths in the description.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-4.md): "The longitudinal slot 16 passes through the rail 10 from its upper side to the lower face 14 and, being viewed along its length, appears in this view as a narrow opening in the upper side of the rail 10, shown schematically." Application text (draft/09-claims.md, claim 1): "a longitudinal slot extending through the rail from the upper face to the lower face"; (draft/08-detailed-description.md): "A straight longitudinal slot 16 (FIG. 2) runs through the rail 10 from the upper face 12 to the lower face 14". Inventor passage (input/disclosure.md): "A straight longitudinal slot runs through the rail." No inventor passage describes the slot's appearance at, or runout to, the rail end.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-4.md, delete the sentence "The longitudinal slot 16 passes through the rail 10 from its upper side to the lower face 14 and, being viewed along its length, appears in this view as a narrow opening in the upper side of the rail 10, shown schematically." FIG. 4 is an unsectioned end elevation and does not need to show the slot; the slot is already shown in FIG. 2, FIG. 3, FIG. 5 and FIG. 7.

findings.title: Numeral 16 used in the FIG. 4 brief but omitted from that figure's numeral list
findings.where: figures/FIG-4.md, body text versus "## Numerals shown on this figure"
findings.detail: The body of the FIG. 4 brief calls out the longitudinal slot 16, but the figure's numeral list contains only 10, 14, 30, 32, 40, 90 and 92. The list and the body must agree so that every numeral shown is accounted for and no numeral is placed on the sheet without a ledger entry for that view.
findings.evidence: Candidate body (figures/FIG-4.md): "The longitudinal slot 16 passes through the rail 10 ...". Candidate list (figures/FIG-4.md): "- 10: rail / - 14: lower face / - 30: fence / - 32: downwardly projecting portion / - 40: spacer plate / - 90: workpiece / - 92: workpiece edge" (no entry for 16).
findings.fix: Adopt the deletion of the slot sentence given for the FIG. 4 geometry finding, after which no change to the list is required. If instead the slot is retained in FIG. 4, add the line "- 16: longitudinal slot" to the "Numerals shown on this figure" list in figures/FIG-4.md between the entries for 14 and 30.

findings.title: FIG. 1 shows an unidentified round body above each guide carriage
findings.where: figures/FIG-1.md, final paragraph of the view description and its numeral list
findings.detail: FIG. 1 depicts a structure above each carriage that carries no reference numeral and is never tied to any part in the description's FIG. 1 discussion, so the reader cannot identify it. The part is source-supported (each carriage has a threaded clamp knob above the rail), so the cure is to label it rather than remove it.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-1.md): "Each guide carriage is shown schematically as a plain block. A plain round body stands above each of the two blocks, shown schematically." The FIG. 1 numeral list contains only 10, 30, 32, 50, 70, 90, 92. Inventor passage (input/disclosure.md): "Each carriage has a threaded clamp knob above the rail."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-1.md, change the sentence to "A clamp knob 58 stands above the first guide carriage 50 and a clamp knob 78 stands above the second guide carriage 70, each shown schematically as a plain round body." and add "- 58: clamp knob of the first guide carriage" and "- 78: clamp knob of the second guide carriage" to the figure's numeral list. In draft/08-detailed-description.md, change "a clamp knob 58 (FIG. 5) on the first guide carriage 50 and a clamp knob 78 (FIG. 3) on the second guide carriage 70" to "a clamp knob 58 (FIGS. 1 and 5) on the first guide carriage 50 and a clamp knob 78 (FIGS. 1 and 3) on the second guide carriage 70".

findings.where: figures/FIG-4.md, paragraph describing the rail 10 and longitudinal slot 16
findings.detail: The sentence is self-contradictory and contradicts the rest of the application: it first says the slot passes through the rail from the upper side to the lower face 14, then says that in this end-on elevation it appears as "a narrow opening in the upper side of the rail 10", which depicts a blind groove rather than a through slot. How the slot terminates or runs out at the rail end, and whether it breaks the upper side only, is an end-face geometry statement that the disclosure never makes, and the through character of the slot is required by claim 1 and by the shank and drill-bit paths in the description.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-4.md): "The longitudinal slot 16 passes through the rail 10 from its upper side to the lower face 14 and, being viewed along its length, appears in this view as a narrow opening in the upper side of the rail 10, shown schematically." Application text (draft/09-claims.md, claim 1): "a longitudinal slot extending through the rail from the upper face to the lower face"; (draft/08-detailed-description.md): "A straight longitudinal slot 16 (FIG. 2) runs through the rail 10 from the upper face 12 to the lower face 14". Inventor passage (input/disclosure.md): "A straight longitudinal slot runs through the rail." No inventor passage describes the slot's appearance at, or runout to, the rail end.
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-4.md, delete the sentence "The longitudinal slot 16 passes through the rail 10 from its upper side to the lower face 14 and, being viewed along its length, appears in this view as a narrow opening in the upper side of the rail 10, shown schematically." FIG. 4 is an unsectioned end elevation and does not need to show the slot; the slot is already shown in FIG. 2, FIG. 3, FIG. 5 and FIG. 7.

findings.title: Numeral 16 used in the FIG. 4 brief but omitted from that figure's numeral list
findings.where: figures/FIG-4.md, body text versus "## Numerals shown on this figure"
findings.detail: The body of the FIG. 4 brief calls out the longitudinal slot 16, but the figure's numeral list contains only 10, 14, 30, 32, 40, 90 and 92. The list and the body must agree so that every numeral shown is accounted for and no numeral is placed on the sheet without a ledger entry for that view.
findings.evidence: Candidate body (figures/FIG-4.md): "The longitudinal slot 16 passes through the rail 10 ...". Candidate list (figures/FIG-4.md): "- 10: rail / - 14: lower face / - 30: fence / - 32: downwardly projecting portion / - 40: spacer plate / - 90: workpiece / - 92: workpiece edge" (no entry for 16).
findings.fix: Adopt the deletion of the slot sentence given for the FIG. 4 geometry finding, after which no change to the list is required. If instead the slot is retained in FIG. 4, add the line "- 16: longitudinal slot" to the "Numerals shown on this figure" list in figures/FIG-4.md between the entries for 14 and 30.

findings.title: FIG. 1 shows an unidentified round body above each guide carriage
findings.where: figures/FIG-1.md, final paragraph of the view description and its numeral list
findings.detail: FIG. 1 depicts a structure above each carriage that carries no reference numeral and is never tied to any part in the description's FIG. 1 discussion, so the reader cannot identify it. The part is source-supported (each carriage has a threaded clamp knob above the rail), so the cure is to label it rather than remove it.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-1.md): "Each guide carriage is shown schematically as a plain block. A plain round body stands above each of the two blocks, shown schematically." The FIG. 1 numeral list contains only 10, 30, 32, 50, 70, 90, 92. Inventor passage (input/disclosure.md): "Each carriage has a threaded clamp knob above the rail."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-1.md, change the sentence to "A clamp knob 58 stands above the first guide carriage 50 and a clamp knob 78 stands above the second guide carriage 70, each shown schematically as a plain round body." and add "- 58: clamp knob of the first guide carriage" and "- 78: clamp knob of the second guide carriage" to the figure's numeral list. In draft/08-detailed-description.md, change "a clamp knob 58 (FIG. 5) on the first guide carriage 50 and a clamp knob 78 (FIG. 3) on the second guide carriage 70" to "a clamp knob 58 (FIGS. 1 and 5) on the first guide carriage 50 and a clamp knob 78 (FIGS. 1 and 3) on the second guide carriage 70".
